verdicts.summary: Both steer callers (message dispatch and promote-to-steer) now fail before any state is persisted, so the queued run stays queued and held.
verdicts.scenario: Promote-to-steer (7811) cancels the queued run in events (7770-7809) and then calls dispatchSteerIntoRun. After Stop, the run_interrupt_request item exists, so stopReachedRun is true and 3963 returns a dispatch error. The cancel events are only in the per-command events Ref, so the failed command does not persist them. I also checked the second caller, message.dispatch at 4975, which hits the same guard. The delegated-completion path is the already-reported finding 0.

verdicts.summary: The downgrade to queue_after_active correctly queues the message and releases holds. The new run and hold release flow through the normal queue path.
verdicts.scenario: After Stop with holdQueue, a plain user send from web with deliveryIntent auto resolves to steer_active, and stopReachedRun is true, so dispatchMode becomes queue_after_active. The steer branch at 4974 is skipped. startsOrQueuesRun is true (5022-5025), activeRun is the still-running stopped run, so shouldQueue is true. The send is user-created from web, so heldRunsToRelease picks up the held queued runs. I found no path where the downgrade leaves the message dropped or the queue held.
